content: IR eval harness libraries are all too heavy for a light pure-Python PyPI CLI: ranx 0.3.21 requires numba>=0.54.1 (JIT, huge wheel, first-call compile latency) + numpy + scipy et al - disqualified; ir-measures 0.4.3 has HARD dependency on pytrec-eval-terrier>=0.5.5 (C extension fork); pytrec_eval itself is a C extension requiring compilation (prebuilt wheels exist for common platforms only). None fit SIF's pure-Python constraint. SIF benchmark.py already has pure-Python precision@k, recall@k, MRR + fixture validation; the missing nDCG@k and MAP are ~40 lines of pure Python - pytrec_eval paper itself notes native Python is competitive for short rankings (5+ docs), and personal-KB benches (dozens of queries x top-10) are far below any perf threshold. Recommendation: extend in-house metrics (nDCG@k with graded relevance, MAP), no new dependency; cross-check numbers once against ir-measures in a dev-only scratch env if desired.
